items.stem: A team reports their claims model is '94% accurate' and concludes it is responsible to deploy. Why is that conclusion unsound?

options.text: Accuracy says nothing about who the errors fall on, or about privacy, transparency and oversight
options.rationale: Correct: responsible AI spans fairness, privacy, transparency and accountability, not a single accuracy number.

options.text: Because 94% is too low for any deployment
options.rationale: There is no universal accuracy threshold; the issue is the other principles are unexamined.

options.text: Because accuracy cannot be measured for text models
options.rationale: Accuracy can be measured; the point is it is insufficient.

options.text: Because responsible AI forbids automated decisions
options.rationale: Responsible AI permits automation with appropriate controls.

items.explanation: Correct: responsible AI spans fairness, privacy, transparency and accountability, not a single accuracy number.

items.stem: Which TWO are organisational (rather than technical) controls for responsible AI? (Select TWO.)

options.text: A documented accountability owner for each deployed model
options.rationale: Correct: assigning accountability is an organisational control.

options.text: An approval policy with a responsible-AI review gate before launch
options.rationale: Correct: policy and review gates are organisational controls.

options.text: A guardrail classifier that blocks unsafe generations
Automated drift monitoring on input distributions

items.explanation: Correct: assigning accountability is an organisational control.

options.text: It misrepresents reliability and discourages the user oversight the system depends on
options.rationale: Correct: transparency requires honest communication of limitations.
Overstating reliability undermines oversight and transparency.
The issue is transparency, not copyright.

options.text: It only matters if the model is open source
options.rationale: It applies regardless of model provenance.
